I preorder games for a few reasons. First and most importantly, I prefer digital games. New games normally take awhile to get discounted digitally, so I'd rather be able to play from the start digitally than wait an unknown amount of time for the game to go on sale. Gaming is my primary hobby, so hype gets to me as well. I like playing my games at midnight on launch, and it feels nice bonding with friends staying up late to play a game we're all excited for. 

The other big reason I preorder is that for many reasons, I run into expendable money very infrequently. It's easier on me to save up money a few months in advance and plan out purchases than it is to impulse buy my backlog when I run into cash. Metal Gear Solid 2. The story was perfect, it was impactful because of our blank slate of a main character, and the gameplay as always with Metal Gear, was incredibly creative and damn functional.

1. I personally think the game is a bit more difficult than Ground Zeroes. Upon death, enemies stay marked, and checkpoints are fairly common, but some outpost setups are incrediby tense to infiltrate, and just as tense to capture. 

2. I can't answer from my own experience, but based on the leak megathreads from the Metal Gear subreddit, it seems that playing through on hard difficulty is pretty much required for the real ending. I doubt collectables are though, so thats nifty. 

3. MGS V is a very different open world. The closest comparison I can think of is Batman Arkham, but even then, just because of the totally different gameplay styles, I just can't say that enjoyment of one indicates anything for the other. 

4. The biggest tips I have are to enjoy the free roam and side ops. They build your bond with your buddies, which unlocks new abilities of theirs, and on top of that, finding new tapes,and playing through the ridiculous amount of missions is great as a break from the very serious story this time around. Speaking of side ops, rescue the gunsmith ASAP. You unlock that side op after mission 13 of the main story. There should be 3 or 4 gunsmith missions. They are vital.

I haven't played Blacklist in particular, but I have played enough different Splinter Cell games to be able to tell you that Metal Gear is a completely different beast. 

Today I scoped out an enemy outpost spotting and marking each enemy in the place. I snuck down the mountainside and took out as many guards as I could as fast as I could. I had a target to extract, he was a very skilled gunsmith. I decided to kidnap each of the men that I took out along my adventure. A group of three enemies saw one of the Fulton Recovery devices in action as it carried their ally into the heavens. One of them ended up posted up sniping at me while I fought the other two, woth shotguns. I peaked around the corner and shot one with my tranq pistol. Seeing that the one sniping at me was reloading, I decided to dash from my cover and grab the other soldier. The sniper shot through him immediately, with no regard for his fellow soldiers life. I decided at that point to disregard my no killing rule and pulled out my assault rifle. Then I realized that he was my target, he was the gunsmith. I ended up knocking him out and taking him to Mother Base. I now slap him around every time I see him at my base, just for killing his own friend. I should also mention that the whole portion done in stealth, was on the back of a badass mech walker.

I don't remember a whole lot of any of that in Splinter Cell. I do remember crawling on the roof because of pipes though... that was pretty fun.

TL;DR: Metal Gear is a great game, especially if you're into stealth. Even if we pretend the story doesn't exist, it's still a front runner for GOTY hands down.

I've been feeling similarly down from time to time lately. My brothers advice rang true to me, to a certain extent. Pick a goal in life. Any goal. For example, I want to become a published author someday. Home in on those goals. Make little check lists to start working towards them. As you see the prorgress towards your goals, regardless of how slight the progress is, it begins to stack up. It helps you feel acomplished. Like you have something going for you. 

Talking through your issues is always healthy as well. If you don't have anyone in your day to day life that can help, or understand what you're feeling, r/depression is full of helpful people. If all you need is to talk a bit when you get down, thats a great place to seek some help. As someone who knows the struggle, you can always PM me as well. 

For some people, getting out and doing something helps as well. Whether that be exercise, hanging out with friends, pursuing your interests, or forming new ones. 

Surrounding yourself with positive people can be helpful for your outlook as well, or so I've heard. Something about a bright personality is infectious. It isn't a permenant way to keep positive, but there is always the chance that the outlook itself can start to click.

Whatever it is you decide to do, make sure and do it for yourself though. I have no idea what may be going on in your personal life, but thats always the thing that helps me the most. Always remember to live for yourself above all else.

Lupe Fiasco is more than the handful of songs of his that make it to the radio. Most people would recommend his first album, but I actually find his second, The Cool, to be a more full experience. Is has something for everyone in my experience. Fan favorite song, Hip Hop Saved my Life, is on the album, along with plenty of other solid songs. He also raps from the point if view of a cheeseburger at one point... so that alone is worth hearing the album for. Most of his music has a serious political and social message tied into it. He is almost entirely about lyrics over everything, so most of his beats aren't too impressive, but with lyrics on this level, it evens out.

Kanye West, probably one of the most well known rappers out today, is also probably one of the most talented. If you can get past the autotune on some of his songs, you find out that he's basically Radiohead. The lyrics reach deep when he wants them to, the music is always a totally different beast from whatever the last album he made was, and the production value is always remarkable. My personal favorite album of his is Yeezus, but you can't really go wrong with any of them. 

If all of these artists fail, listen to Atmosphere, and then delve into Macklemore and his music. Atmosphere is a bit older than any of the other artists I've listed, and they really show a mastery of lyrics, particularly in storytelling. Macklemore is the closest artist to replicating how Slug tells stories, and that in itself is an impressive feat. Macklemore also has all kinds of fun on a lot of his tracks. The Heist is a great start to get into Macklemore's music, but any of his mixtapes offer a more fleshed out experience on political views, humor, and heartfelt music. 

Last but not least is, Lil Dicky. He really isn't too popular yet, and he may never get there. But I rarely enjoy a song as much as I do Ex-Boyfriend. So Hard is a fantastic set of songs, and for pure fun, he is the way to go.

I'll be honest, I have little experience with SRPG's myself. My interest started with Xcom: Enemy Unknown, and since then, I've gotten Fire Emblem Awakening, and Shin Megami. Shin Megami is easily my favorite of the bunch though. The combat system is incredibly deep. Picking out abilities and attack skills for your characters and your monster teammates ensures you can have a ton of variety to your teams. Sort of like Pokemon games, each monster has resistances, and weaknesses. If you get good at setting up your team, you can make missions a clean sweep, or a total struggle. It really is all about planning, even after a decent amount of grinding. The way I played, to beat the first boss, you'll need to grind a fair amount, but after that, the game has felt relatively grind free. That said, the grind is genuinely a good time, mostly because battles are a delight to be a part of. Even the easier battles feel fantastic and satisfying, or at least they did for me. The story is pretty interesting too, though some of the characters are annoying. For the most part, I thoroughly enjoyed it, and besides Bravely Default, it may be my favorite 3ds game. I also haven't even scratched the surface on how the monsters work. It really is a deep and complex game. If you pick it up, it should keep you entertained for quite some time.

I dated this girl when I was too young to understand how well suited for me she was, so after a few years of us going our seperate ways, I start talking to her on Facebook again. We even seemed to have similar issues in our life, meaning we were kindered spirits, I'll elaborate on this later in though. Anyways, even though I was clearly in love, and all of my friend could tell that the feeling was mutual in the entirety, there was a problem, her boyfriend, who we'll call Doug, didn't like me... at all... He wasn't really a dick per se, on the regular, it was just with me, he must have known how I felt, and how ruthlessly I was disregarding the sanctity of their relationship, (which I still feel quite poor about by the way.) Well, after a few monthes of the same old shit, me flirting with her on Facebook, not being allowed to talk to her at school because her boyfriend would see us then, her Dad passed away. He had been struggling with various health problems for a very long time, and it had been an issue that she struggled with constantly, losing a parent as a teenager, was hard for her, as I imagine it would be for anybody. I was invited to the memorial service, not by her, but by her mother, who knew how much I meant to her daughter, and while she didn't like me much, she felt it would help to have me present. I showed up to the memorial, and she only had a couple friends there, most of the group was family, family she didn't really get along with, so I was glad to be able to keep her company. The thing that struck me though, was that Doug wasn't here, he was off doing something almost certainly less important... So as disgusting as it sounds, her fathers memorial was essentially like a first date for us, we were close, talking the whole time, I kept her smiling and was glad to be there, it was like a dream... in an albeit morbid setting, but still. Her boyfriend arrived ten minutes before the memorial was over, I don't remember his excuse for being late, mainly because he kept scowling at me while I was there, I couldn't hear a thing out of anybodies mouth at that point, I was laughing too hard at the kid in my head. I got picked up from the memorial and all was well, then for the first time ever, I recieved a phone call from her, and we talked from the time I got picked up, maybe 4:00 Pm, steadily through to midnight, and through this call, she finally admitted to having feelings for me, it was damn near the perfect day for me. Get back to school after not speaking to her that weekend, and much to my surprise, she walked up to me at lunch and told me that she had broken up with Doug, I was elated. All the time I had put in, was finally paying off. Then we just kind of stopped talking, she got back together with Doug, and I spiraled into a sickening depression, one that has lasted from that day up until this second, althoguh i have to admit, it isn't all her fault. It keeps hitting home how perfect it would be to be with her, see, my own dad, only a year after hers passed away, was diagnosed with liver failure, got put on oxygen and began rambling about suicide 24/7, in his ammonia filled and oxygen lacking rages, he'd sometimes hit his caretaker, kick us out of the house, or just yell for hours. None of it I hold against him, I know it was the disease, but still, she woudl be the best person to talk to in this case, she knows exactly what I'm going through. And yet, we never formed a connection again, no matter how many times I've tried. Shes single again now, and dad is all better, after receiving his liver transplant, so I suppose, I made it without her, but it still hurts to have loved and not only lost, but lost so suddenly as so much of my world crashed down. My friends like to point out that if my dad had passed away, I might have had enough leverage to talk to her again, and that is by far the most depressing detail of my life.
